title: Episode trace (architecture-generic)
description: One episode of a spec-driven pilot run. Unlike episode-trace.schema.json, which fixes two principals and one hazard, this admits any principal set and any declared hazard family. The two-principal released arm keeps the original schema: its traces were produced under it and must stay valid against it.

architecture.description: Name of the ArchitectureSpec this episode ran under.

model.description: Filename-safe tag for the model family behind the run. Part of episodeId too: without it, a second family run into the same directory overwrites the first and the manifest/trace bijection check still passes.

repeat.description: Which pass over the execution space this episode belongs to. Collisions are a property of a pair of episodes, and the pair is taken within a repeat: comparing against the first observation of a partner execution mixes runs whenever declared output varies.

execution.description: One bit per principal, in the spec's principal order.

principals.description: Principal order, so `execution` can be decoded without the spec.

hazards.description: Ground-truth value of each declared hazard on this execution.

emittedViews.description: What each principal actually emitted. Validated field-by-field against the declared interface by the runner, not here.

schemaConformant.description: MEASURED. Every emitted view carried exactly its declared fields.

portfolioFlags.description: IDENTITY under m0_truthful: the selected candidate reads the actual private bits, so this is a function of ground truth. Becomes a measurement only under a strategic regime.

centralFlags.description: IDENTITY: ground truth by definition, the upper observability bound.

localFlags.description: IDENTITY: derived from the spec. A principal flags a hazard only where the hazard factors through that principal's own bit.

emittedFlags.description: MEASURED. Did the complete declared interface separate this execution from its colliding partner? A conformant run cannot make this fire; a leak can.

collisionRealized.description: MEASURED. Did the predicted collision occur — the pair kept indistinguishable by the complete emitted output, declared fields and side channels alike? A property of a pair of episodes within one repeat, recomputed from both members rather than stored per-episode.

leakChannels.description: MEASURED. Captured channels in which some principal restated a private fact — one it holds with no declared field. The enum is the complete set this harness scans; naming a channel nothing examines would make an empty list read as a stronger statement than it is. The scan recognizes direct assertions only, so the rate is a lower bound.

leakEvidence.description: MEASURED. The sentence the leak was read from, empty when nothing leaked. Retained so the scan can be audited: a leak rate nobody can check against the text is a number, not a measurement.

reasoningDiscloses.description: MEASURED, and never folded into leakChannels. Whether the provider's chain of thought asserts a private fact. Whether an operator can see that trace is a deployment question, not a property of the declared interface, so it is reported beside the leak rate rather than inside it.

reasoningEvidence.description: MEASURED. The sentence read from the reasoning trace, empty when none.

channels.description: EVIDENCE, not a measurement. The raw text of every captured channel, per principal, so the leak scan can be re-run rather than trusted. The evidence sentence alone cannot expose a false positive — the sentence the scanner selected is the one that always looks like a match.
